methodFirst: The true first move is METHOD, not a text. Before Miller laid a single prophetic link he laid the KEY: "I determined to lay aside all my prepossessions, to thoroughly compare Scripture with Scripture, and to pursue its study in a regular and methodical manner. I commenced with Genesis, and read verse by verse" (WMAD 6.1; verbatim in MWM 69.3, SLWM 48.1). The licensing premise: "if the Bible was the word of God, every thing contained therein might be understood, and all its parts be made to harmonize" (WMAD 5.1); he was "fully satisfied that it is its own interpreter" (WMAD 6.1). The method is codified in the 14 Rules, whose hinge is Rule V — "Scripture must be its own expositor, since it is a rule of itself" (MWV1 20.10 / MWM 70.6) — and whose figure-rule is "trace your figurative word through your Bible, and where you find it explained, put it on your figure" (MWV1 22.5). Brother Miller's Dream makes it canonical: the casket = the advent truths, but "the key attached" = "his manner of interpreting the prophetic Word — Comparing scripture with scripture — the Bible its own interpreter. With this key Bro. Miller opened the casket" (BMD 3.3). The key precedes the jewels, and the jewels are only "beautifully arranged in their several places" (the chain in proper ORDER) because the key opened them. Method is link zero; strip it out and the chain dissolves into private opinion.

startingPoint.answer: One STARTS with the method (the key), then physically with Genesis 1 — reading verse by verse straight through, comparing Scripture with Scripture and letting the Bible define its own figures via Cruden's Concordance. The chain is BUILT, not jumped to. When a prophetic TEXT must be named as the doorway, it is Daniel 8:14 ('Unto 2300 days, then shall the sanctuary be cleansed') — 'The prophecy which seemed most clearly to reveal the time of the second advent' (GC 324.3). But in Miller's own account the FIRST time-prophecy to convince him was the 'seven times'/2520, and the 2300 days came next as the confirming witness: 'I was satisfied that the seven times terminated in 1843. Then I came to the 2300 days; they brought me to the same conclusion' (TSAM 65.3).
startingPoint.rationale: Miller's autobiography is explicit that he 'commenced with no expectation of finding the time of the Savior's coming' (WMAD 12.1) — he did not start FROM a prophecy of the advent; the advent doctrine was the RESULT of the method applied from Genesis forward. So the genuine starting point is the method-plus-Genesis. As an interpretive doorway into the time-chain specifically, Daniel 8:14 is primary because everything hangs on finding 'the correct starting point for the 2300 days' (GC 324.3) — and that starting point is supplied by the 70 weeks of Daniel 9, dated from the 457 BC decree, which 'seal (or make sure) the vision' (MWV1 46.2). Daniel 2 is the structural spine that legitimizes reading Daniel 8's little horn as Rome ('these three visions are but one prophecy', MWV1 188.2), but it is not itself the time-doorway.

chainLinks.link: LINK 0 — The KEY (method) laid first: lay aside prepossessions, compare Scripture with Scripture, the Bible is its own interpreter; begin at Genesis and read verse by verse with a concordance.
chainLinks.why: This is the move BEFORE any doctrine. Miller's whole structure depends on the premise that an inspired Bible must be self-consistent and intelligible (WMAD 5.1). The casket allegory fixes method as the key that opens everything (BMD 3.3). The 14 Rules (esp. Rule V) are the written form of this practice.

chainLinks.link: The Bible is a harmonious system of revealed truth, to be read as literally as makes good sense; every figure/metaphor is either explained in its context or defined elsewhere in Scripture.
chainLinks.why: Direct fruit of the method applied for two years from Genesis. This conclusion is what makes prophecy interpretable at all — figures get fixed meanings from the Bible itself, not from the commentator (WMAD 6.1; MWV1 33.1).

chainLinks.link: Christ's second coming is PERSONAL and PRE-millennial, literal and visible in the clouds — demolishing the popular temporal/spiritual millennium and the Jews' return.
chainLinks.why: Because the unfulfilled-prophecy figures are 'as clearly expressed' as the ones literally fulfilled at the first advent, the literalizing method forces a literal future advent and rules out a prior temporal millennium (WMAD 6.2). This clears the ground so the advent can be 'a continually expected event' (WMAD 9.1).

chainLinks.link: Only FOUR universal monarchies precede God's everlasting kingdom; three are past (Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece), Rome is in its last state — Daniel 2's image is the spine, and Daniel 2, 7, and 8 are ONE prophecy repeated.
chainLinks.why: Establishes the world is near its end and supplies the historical skeleton. Critically, Miller argues 'these three visions are but one prophecy' so the little horn of Daniel 8 must be Rome, not Antiochus — without this, the 2300-day doorway collapses (MWV1 188.2; WMAD 9.1).

chainLinks.link: Prophetic time is real and reckonable: a day stands for a year (Num 14:34; Ezek 4:6), proven by the many literal-time prophecies already fulfilled (the flood days, the 400 years, the 70 weeks = 490 years, the 1260 days = 1260 years).
chainLinks.why: The chronological key. Miller validates the day-year principle inductively from already-fulfilled time prophecies (WMAD 9.2, 11.1), and only THEN trusts it to measure the unfulfilled periods extending to the advent (WMAD 10.1).

chainLinks.link: Several prophetic periods all extend to the advent and converge on 1843: the 'seven times'/2520 (from 677 BC), the 2300 days (from 457 BC), and the 1335 days (from AD 508).
chainLinks.why: In Miller's own testimony the 'seven times' convinced him FIRST and the 2300 days came next as a corroborating witness landing on the same date: 'I was satisfied that the seven times terminated in 1843. Then I came to the 2300 days; they brought me to the same conclusion' (TSAM 65.3; cf. WMAD 11.2; MWV1 46.1).

chainLinks.link: The DOORWAY prophecy of the time-chain: Daniel 8:14, 'Unto 2300 days, then shall the sanctuary be cleansed' — the longest period, reaching to the advent.
chainLinks.why: This is the text that 'most clearly' reveals the time of the advent (GC 324.3). Everything now hinges on one question: where do the 2300 days START? (MWV1 46.2). It is the keystone of Miller's 'four pillars' (MWV1 188.2).

chainLinks.link: The 70 weeks (Daniel 9:24–27) are 'cut off' from the 2300 days and share its starting point — the decree to restore Jerusalem, 457 BC — fixing the commencement of the whole vision.
chainLinks.why: Gabriel gave the 70 weeks expressly to 'seal (or make sure) the vision', giving 'a clue to know when his vision of the ram and he-goat began' (MWV1 46.2). The 490 years ran out in AD 33; so the same start (457 BC) gives the 2300. This is the load-bearing joint Miller's critics attacked first because it carries the whole argument (MWV1 188.2).

chainLinks.link: 457 BC + 2300 years = 1843/44: the cleansing of the sanctuary and the glorious appearing of Christ; convergence of all periods and the close of probation.
chainLinks.why: Arithmetic forced by the prior links: 'If 490 days were fulfilled in the year A.D. 33... when will 1810 days afterwards be fulfilled in the same manner? Answer, 1843' (MWV1 46.2). 'If, then, the correct starting point could be found for the 2300 days... the time of the second advent could be readily ascertained' (GC 324.3). This is the climax the casket's jewels reflect (BMD 3.3).

keyQuotes.quote: I then devoted myself to prayer and to the reading of the word. I determined to lay aside all my prepossessions, to thoroughly compare Scripture with Scripture, and to pursue its study in a regular and methodical manner. I commenced with Genesis, and read verse by verse... and was fully satisfied that it is its own interpreter.

I replied that if the Bible was the word of God, every thing contained therein might be understood, and all its parts be made to harmonize... if he would give me time, I would harmonize all these apparent contradictions, to my own satisfaction, or I would be a Deist still.

The “key attached” was his manner of interpreting the prophetic Word - Comparing scripture with scripture - the Bible its own interpreter. With this key Bro. Miller opened the “casket,” or the great truth of the advent to the world... jewels... beautifully arranged in their several places in the casket; and thus arranged they reflected a light and glory.

Scripture must be its own expositor, since it is a rule of itself. If I depend on a teacher to expound it to me, and he should guess at its meaning, or desire to have it so on account of his sectarian creed... then his guessing, desire, creed or wisdom, is my rule, and not the Bible.

To learn the true meaning of figures, trace your figurative word through your Bible, and where you find it explained, put it on your figure, and if it makes good sense you need look no further, if not, look again.

I began at Genesis, and read on slowly; and when I came to a text that I could not understand, I searched through the Bible to find out what it meant... I was satisfied that the seven times terminated in 1843. Then I came to the 2300 days; they brought me to the same conclusion.

I commenced their study with no expectation of finding the time of the Savior’s coming, and I could at first hardly believe the result to which I had arrived; but the evidence struck me with such force, that I could not resist my convictions.

If, then, the 70 weeks were a part of the vision of the ram and he-goat, and given... for the express purpose of showing the beginning of the vision... If 490 days were fulfilled in the year A.D. 33, by being so many years, when will 1810 days afterwards be fulfilled in the same manner? Answer, 1843.

a few of his main attacks on my “four pillars,” as he calls them. 1. The 2300 days, Daniel 8:13, 14... my argument that the three visions, had at three several times, are but one prophecy... and if this be true, then the little horn, instead of being Antiochus, must be the Roman kingdom.

The prophecy which seemed most clearly to reveal the time of the second advent was that of Daniel 8:14... Following his rule of making Scripture its own interpreter, Miller learned that a day in symbolic prophecy represents a year... If, then, the correct starting point could be found for the 2300 days, he concluded that the time of the second advent could be readily ascertained.

only four universal monarchies are any where predicted in the Bible to precede the setting up of God’s everlasting kingdom; that three of those had passed away, - Babylon, Medo-Persia, and Grecia, - and that the fourth, Rome, had already passed into its last state.

the 2300 days commenced with the seventy weeks, which the best chronologers dated from B. C. 457... Reckoning all these prophetic periods from the several dates assigned by the best chronologers... they all would terminate together, about A. D. 1843.

uncertainties: Order of subjective discovery vs. logical order of the chain: In TSAM 65.3 Miller says the 'seven times'/2520 convinced him FIRST and the 2300 days came as confirmation — yet in his published lectures and in GC 324.3 the 2300 days/Dan 8:14 is presented as the primary doorway and the 2520 as a converging witness. The 'first link' therefore differs depending on whether one means Miller's personal sequence of conviction or the expository order he taught.

Whether Daniel 2 should count as a distinct CHAIN LINK or as part of the method/framework. Miller treats Dan 2, 7, 8 as 'one prophecy' (MWV1 188.2) and uses Dan 2 as the spine that licenses identifying Dan 8's little horn as Rome, but he does not derive a time-period from Dan 2 itself — so its status is structural/foundational rather than a time-link.

The 'daily' (Dan 8:13) and the AD 508 starting point for the 1335 days rest on Miller's reading of 'the daily' = Paganism (TSAM 66.2-3), which is interpretively the softest joint in the chain and was later contested among Adventists; sources here are Miller's own reasoning rather than independent confirmation.

Exact decree/year for the 70 weeks: Miller follows 'the best chronologers' at 457 BC (Artaxerxes' decree) but in WMAD 11.2 also dates the 2520 from 677 BC (Manasseh's captivity); the multiple anchor-dates show the chronology depends on then-current historical sources rather than the Bible alone, a dependence Miller's method is in tension with.

The page-12 'laid by all commentaries' quotation cited in the 14-Rules study (attributed to Works vol. 1 p.12) did not surface verbatim under MWV1 12 in this search session; the substance is fully corroborated by WMAD 6.1 and MWM 69.3, but the exact MWV1 refcode for that specific wording was not re-verified here.
